'''Boris (Boaz) Abramovich Trakhtenbrot''' ({{langx|ru|Борис Авраамович Трахтенброт}}, {{langx|he|בועז טרכטנברוט}}; 19 February 1921 – 19 September 2016) was a Russian-Israeli [[mathematician]] in [[mathematical logic|logic]], [[algorithm]]s, [[theory of computation]], and [[cybernetics]].

==Biography==
Trakhtenbrot was born into a Jewish family in [[Tîrnova, Dondușeni|Brichevo]], northern [[Bessarabia]] (now Tîrnova, [[Moldova]]).<ref name="trakhJG">{{cite encyclopedia|encyclopedia=Russian Jewish Encyclopedia|title=Surnames starting with the letter T|translator1-first=Josif|translator1-last=Charny|translator2-first=Vitaly|translator2-last=Charny|date=1995|location=Moscow|url=http://jewishgen.org/belarus/rje_t.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030415025359/http://www.jewishgen.org/belarus/rje_t.htm|archive-date=15 April 2003}}</ref> He studied at the [[Ion Creangă State Pedagogical University|Moldovan State Pedagogical Institute]] in [[Chișinău|Kishinev]], [[Chernivtsi University]], and the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine|Ukrainian Academy of Science]]'s Mathematical Institute, completing a Ph.D. at the latter institution in 1950.{{r|TAU}}

He worked at [[Akademgorodok]], [[Novosibirsk]] during the 1960s and 1970s.<ref name="trakhErshov">{{cite web|website=Архив академика А.П. Ершова|language=ru|script-title=ru:Борис Абрамович Трахтенброт|trans-title=Boris A. Trakhtenbrot|url=http://www.ershov.ras.ru/archive/eaman.asp?pplid=1758&?lang=2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726013528/http://www.ershov.ras.ru/archive/eaman.asp?pplid=1758&%3Flang=2|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 July 2011}}</ref><ref name="trakhCSHistory">{{cite web|title=History of Computing in Russia|script-title=ru:Борис Авраамович Трахтенброт|trans-title=Boris Avraamovich Trahtenbrot|url=http://cshistory.nsu.ru/obj1181/INTERFACE.htm|language=ru|access-date=22 January 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080429161306/http://cshistory.nsu.ru/obj1181/INTERFACE.htm|archive-date=29 April 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1964 Trakhtenbrot discovered and proved a fundamental result in [[theoretical computer science]] called the [[gap theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Boris Trakhtenbrot|title=Turing computations with logarithmic delay|journal=[[Algebra i Logika|Algebra and Logic]]|language=ru|volume=3|issue=4|pages= 33–48|year=1964}}</ref> He also discovered and proved the theorem in [[logic]], [[model theory]], and [[computability theory]] now known as [[Trakhtenbrot's theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Boris Trakhtenbrot|title=The Impossibility of an Algorithm for the Decidability Problem on Finite Classes|journal=[[Proceedings of the USSR Academy of Sciences]]|language=ru|volume=70|issue=4|pages= 569–572|year=1950}}</ref> 

After immigrating to [[Israel]] in 1981, he became a professor in the Faculty of [[Exact Science]]s at [[Tel Aviv University]], and continued as [[Professors in the United States#Professor emeritus and emerita|professor emeritus]] until his death. He died on 19 September 2016, at the age of 95.{{r|TAU}}{{r|fisher}}
